# B-Agent Rule 26 Research Incorporation Tracker

Temporary supervisor remediation tracker created 2026-06-17.

Part 1 validator update: new supervisor-verified B reports are executed through
`tools/validator.py execute_report ... --apply` into
`executed-b-agent-research/B###/`. Do not manually move new verified reports
into per-agent `research/executed/` folders or manually update validator-owned
generated reports. Use `auto-generated/-ag-research-tracker.md` as the
validator-generated executed-research coverage view, and use
`execute-rescan-reports`, `execute-confirm-change`, `executed-reassign`, and
`invalidate_execute` for registry repair, intentional post-execution changes,
reassignment, and rework. Do not edit `tools/validator.ini`, queue JSON, lock
files, or generated reports manually. Historical rows below may mention the old
`research/executed` archive flow; treat those as legacy history unless a later
row or current user instruction says otherwise.

## Purpose

Review every B-agent research report under:

- `Agent-B001/research`
- `Agent-B002/research`
- `Agent-B003/research`
- `Agent-B004/research`
- `Agent-B005/research`
- `Agent-B006/research`
- `Agent-B007/research`
- `Agent-B008/research`
- `Agent-B009/research`
- `Agent-B010/research`
- `Agent-B011/research`
- `Agent-B012/research`
- `Agent-B013/research`
- `Agent-B014/research`
- `Agent-B015/research`

The review includes active reports, executed reports, `executed/older` reports, and scratch reports. For each report, the supervisor must compare the research against the relevant by-* target/support documents and either:

- send the reporting B agent an implementation checklist and verify that the agent incorporated every valid behavior, interaction, field/type/global/helper/source-placement, rejected-alternative, historical-assumption, and C++-readiness detail from the report into the by-* docs;
- record that every valid report claim is already present in the relevant by-* docs with the same or greater factual detail after a claim-by-claim comparison; or
- record why a specific omitted detail is stale, superseded, invalid, duplicate, or not applicable.

2026-06-19 workflow change, updated by Part 1 validator workflow: new B reports are not closed by supervisor-side target/support by-* edits by default. After accepting a report direction, the supervisor gives the same B agent a concrete implementation checklist. The B agent applies the accepted target/support by-* edits under normal lease and validation rules. The supervisor then verifies the report, checklist, changed docs, and validation output before marking the tracker row `DONE`, executing the report through `tools/validator.py execute_report ... --apply`, and reassigning the B agent. Supervisor-owned shared files such as assignment ledgers and manual tracker updates remain supervisor work unless the user explicitly changes that ban; validator-owned `auto-generated/-ag-*` reports are refreshed from source metadata and validator commands, not hand-edited.

There is no arbitrary detail cap for Rule 26 incorporation. Do not close a report because the target already has a summary, a shorter restatement, "enough" information, or only the recommendation implemented. Close it only when every valid report detail has been incorporated into by-* docs while preserving the report's factual detail, is already present in the relevant by-* docs at the same or greater factual detail after explicit claim-by-claim comparison, or is explicitly excluded for a documented stale/superseded/invalid/duplicate/not-applicable reason.
Do not describe a closure as "enough detail was incorporated." The expected closure statement is that all valid report details were incorporated, were already present at the same or greater factual detail after claim-by-claim comparison, or were explicitly excluded with concrete reasons. Document size, readability, duplication discomfort, or a target already being above a score gate is not a reason to reduce valid B-agent research detail.
Tracker notes must not use vague completion language as the reason a report is complete. Do not write or rely on compact-summary wording as a completion standard. Completion requires claim-by-claim accounting: incorporated with all valid report details preserved, already present in the relevant by-* docs at the same or greater factual detail, or explicitly excluded with a concrete reason. A `DONE` row must enumerate the report's valid details or point to an explicit per-claim accounting/checklist, plus name the compared/updated by-* docs; naming only broad claim families is not a valid substitute for incorporation.
If a previous tracker note says a report was incorporated, already represented, already carried, already present, or otherwise "sufficient" but only gives a compact summary, treat that as provisional administrative state, not proof that Rule 26 is closed. The row must be expanded during audit or reopened until every valid detail is accounted for. Any previous supervisor wording that implied a detail limit, readability limit, or "enough detail" threshold is invalid and must not be used as completion evidence.

A report is not considered Rule 26 closed merely because its recommendation was implemented, the report was archived, or a brief coverage/documentation summary exists.
All B-agent reports are treated as under-incorporated at tracker intake. Do not assume any executed, older, or scratch report is already represented in by-* documentation until the supervisor has checked it claim-by-claim against the actual by-* docs and verified the same or greater factual detail.
Review order is administrative only. Do not use "recent" versus "older" report location as evidence that one group was more or less incorporated; every B-agent report starts this audit as under-incorporated until proven otherwise by claim-by-claim comparison.

## Rule 26 Audit Override

The previous supervisor wording sometimes treated "already represented" or compact report summaries as closure. That is not acceptable for this audit. A report is only truly closed when the tracker row or a linked checklist accounts for the report claim by claim. Any `DONE` row that does not show that accounting is provisional administrative history, even if it says the target already had the information. Reopen and recheck those rows when encountered.

For this audit, "incorporated" means all valid applicable report details are carried into the relevant by-* documents at report-level factual specificity, with no arbitrary length cap. Only omit a detail when the row records the exact stale, superseded, invalid, duplicate, or not-applicable reason. Do not collapse behavior, interactions, field/type/global/helper/source-placement evidence, rejected alternatives, historical assumptions, or C++ readiness findings into a shorter summary just because the target is already readable.

Supervisor correction: compact-summary wording is not a Rule 26 completion standard. The audit must preserve every valid applicable report detail in the by-* documents, including intermediate evidence, negative checks, rejected alternatives, heuristic/inference rationale, historical assumptions, support-file implications, and C++ readiness reasoning. A report may be closed without patching only when the supervisor has verified the same specific details are already present in the relevant by-* docs at report-level specificity, not merely when a shorter summary or recommendation is present.

2026-06-18 correction: any older row below that says a report was "already represented", "already incorporated", "already carried", "found already present", or similar wording is not proof of Rule 26 completion. Treat those rows as provisional administrative notes and re-open them when encountered unless the row also enumerates the report's concrete valid details or links to a per-claim checklist. The audit assumption is that every B-agent report started under-incorporated; a row can only overcome that assumption by recording the actual claim-by-claim comparison or the patches that carried the missing details into by-* docs.

2026-06-18 supervisor correction: do not use "enough detail", "sufficient detail", broad report-family summaries, readability judgments, or "already represented" shorthand as Rule 26 closure. There is no acceptable reduced-detail threshold. If a row only says the docs had enough information, already carried the information, or only names broad topics without preserving the report's specific valid claims, the row is administrative history and must be re-opened or expanded before it can count as complete.

## Status Legend

- `PENDING`: report is in scope and has not been reviewed for Rule 26 incorporation.
- `IN_REVIEW`: currently being compared against target/support by-* docs.
- `NEEDS_PATCH`: valid research is missing from one or more by-* docs.
- `PATCHED_VALIDATE`: by-* docs were patched and validation is pending.
- `DONE`: Rule 26 incorporation is complete: all valid report details were incorporated by the reporting B agent during the supervisor-issued implementation pass, incorporated by the supervisor only where explicitly allowed, or were already present at the same or greater factual detail after a claim-by-claim comparison; any omitted details are explicitly stale, superseded, invalid, duplicate, or not applicable. The tracker row must enumerate the report's valid details or link/point to a per-claim accounting/checklist, must name the by-* document set that was compared or updated, and must record that the supervisor verified the agent-applied implementation before archive/reassignment for new reports under the 2026-06-19 workflow.
- `REJECTED_RETRY`: active/pending report is incomplete and was returned to the B-agent.
- `STALE`: report was superseded; tracker must explain the newer source.

Rows written before the stricter per-claim wording may still be too category-level. Treat any `DONE` row that only summarizes broad topics and does not enumerate valid details or point to a per-claim checklist as provisionally documented, not as proof of Rule 26 closure. When such a row is revisited, expand it to per-claim accounting or reopen it as `NEEDS_PATCH`/`IN_REVIEW` until every valid report detail is incorporated, already present at same-or-greater factual detail, or explicitly excluded with a concrete reason.
